holidays.name: National Zoo Lovers Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate zoos and the animals living in them. Visit your local zoo, adopt an animal through a sponsorship program, or simply wave at a giraffe and feel good about it.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance popularized through holiday calendars, meant to encourage appreciation for zoos and their role in conservation, education, and research.
holidays.funFact: Giraffes only sleep about 30 minutes to 2 hours a day, often in very short naps, so you might catch one on a very busy schedule.

holidays.name: International Pillow Fight Day
holidays.description: A worldwide day when strangers gather in public squares armed with pillows for gloriously fluffy, feather-flying mayhem. The rules usually say to hit gently and to bring soft pillows only.
holidays.origin: It began as a flash mob-style event organized online in the early 2000s, with the first big coordinated fights happening in 2006. The event became a global phenomenon, held in the first weekend of April in many cities, but is often associated with early April dates including April 8 in some calendars.
holidays.funFact: Organizers typically ask participants to avoid hard pillows and to clean up the feathers afterward, because nothing ruins a fun time like a feather-covered park.

holidays.name: National Empanada Day
holidays.description: A tasty celebration of the stuffed, folded, baked or fried pastry beloved across Latin America, Spain, and the Philippines. Fillings range from beef and cheese to sweet guava.
holidays.origin: A food-calendar observance created to honor the empanada, whose name comes from the Spanish verb 'empanar,' meaning to wrap or coat in bread.
holidays.funFact: Empanadas are believed to date back to medieval Iberia, and a 16th-century Catalan cookbook mentions empanadas filled with seafood.

holidays.name: Buddha's Birthday (Hanamatsuri) in Japan
holidays.description: A flower festival in Japan marking the birth of Siddhartha Gautama. Temples are decorated with blossoms, and visitors ladle sweet tea over small statues of the baby Buddha.
holidays.origin: Observed in Japan on April 8 for centuries, partly because the date lines up with the cherry blossom season, which gives the festival its name, meaning 'flower festival.'
holidays.funFact: The sweet tea poured over the baby Buddha statue is called amacha, and it is made from fermented hydrangea leaves.

holidays.name: Draw a Picture of a Bird Day
holidays.description: A creative holiday that invites everyone, from serious artists to stick-figure enthusiasts, to sketch a bird. Talent is not required, and a wobbly pigeon counts.
holidays.origin: A whimsical unofficial observance in the creative-holiday calendar, meant to encourage art and bird appreciation at the same time.
holidays.funFact: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backward, which makes them a pretty challenging subject to capture in motion.
